checks.name: catalogue rainfall inside the Atlas 14 band, 2-100 y
checks.note: fail, accepted: below the band at 2, 5, 10 y; accepted by Yuri as CH-19 ('Accept, start batch', 2026-11-26); recorded as a finding
checks.rule: 3-hour annual maximum at the study box (rank M / T of M) within Atlas 14 AMS 3-hr 90% band at 2, 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100 years (plan F4)

checks.name: every finished batch run has a record and a water balance within 1%
checks.rule: spec.json, run_run.json and balance.json present, |residual| <= 1% of the rain (FH8), for every finished catalogue and design run

checks.name: depth non-decreasing with return period before the clean-up
checks.rule: share of read cells whose depth_at curve never falls as AEP falls >= 0.99

checks.name: depth non-decreasing in every cell after the clean-up
checks.rule: every read cell non-decreasing after make_non_decreasing; cells changed reported

checks.name: grid route read back equal (Dataset.from_raster)
checks.rule: every delivered cell's knots equal what was written (1e-6 m), same probabilities, same cell count (FH7)

checks.name: point route read back equal (Dataset.from_quantiles)
checks.rule: every asset's knots delivered equal to those written (1e-9) (FH7)

checks.name: point route reads the catalogue's depth (CH-23)
checks.rule: for every asset, CRC's QuantileCurve on the knots at the seven probabilities equals the catalogue's depth_at (1e-9 m)

checks.name: at least 60 catalogue runs before 1 December

notes: F4 storm catalogue and batch: N = 150 catalogue storms, 1000 of 1000 years covered. Depth frequency is empirical (catalogue.depth_at, RainyDay's rank convention), one storm per synthetic year; the largest-rain storm of a year is taken as its worst flood. Grid depth: calibration.run_depth (src/flood_lab/hazard/calibration.py): peak water level less the ground at each 5 m cell's centre 1 m pixel, the ground never below the cell's lowest sub-grid level (CH-20), floored at 0, the definition the constant loss rate was calibrated and FH8 tested on; not read (NaN) where calibration.Frame leaves a cell out: centre pixel in a building footprint, any pixel in a filled pit, centre pixel on mapped water, lowest level below the start water level (CH-16). Whole square, not only the study area. Asset depths: at_assets (1 m pixels; substation lead measure, building wall band). Figures made before the batch completes are rebuilt afterwards (requirements §15).

domain.png: 3-hour ratio map (smoothed mean annual maximum over the study area's, AORC 2002-2025) over the download window, domain B, the study box and the 960 storms of the chosen catalogue, each at the centre of the box-sized window of its largest 3-hour rain (RainyDay's storm location).

rainfall_frequency.png: 3-hour annual maximum rainfall at the study box: the chosen catalogue (960 storms, M = 1000, T = M / rank), the 240- and 480-storm sensitivities, Atlas 14 AMS 3-hr with its 90% band, and AORC observed box maxima at Weibull plotting positions T = (n + 1) / i. Below the band at 2-10 y: fail, accepted (CH-19).

depth_strip.png: Per-cell depth at 10, 100 and 500 years from the catalogue (N = 150 catalogue storms, 1000 of 1000 years covered) beside the 1-hour and 3-hour Atlas 14 design storms of the same return periods.

buildings_wet.png: Buildings of the study area wet at the wall (0.05 m, 0.3 m) at 100 years: the catalogue (N = 150 catalogue storms, 1000 of 1000 years covered; each building's own curve at annual exceedance probability (AEP) 0.01) against each design storm; beside it every design storm with the 5 m cells it wets. Shaded: storms that wet no 5 m cell or whose rain does not exceed the 30 mm/h constant loss rate; since CH-20 and CH-21 (ground never below a cell's lowest sub-grid level) they wet no cell and no building, where before they showed about 2,900 buildings.
wet_runs.png: Number of catalogue runs wetting each read 5 m cell (N = 150 catalogue storms, 1000 of 1000 years covered).
progress.png: Catalogue runs finished per stratum; solver wall time and water-balance residual per finished run (catalogue and design).
